prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1111; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a low-speed collision in a retail parking lot. Insured vehicle reported to have struck the rear quarter panel of the claimant's parked vehicle while reversing from a space. Claimant reports minor neck pain at the scene and was transported by a family member for evaluation. Photos requested from both parties.

Entry 2: Claimant contacted by phone. Claimant states they were seen at an urgent care facility and diagnosed with a concussion, with headaches, light sensitivity, and dizziness reported. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says they are handling the claim directly. Medical records authorization form sent to claimant for signature.

Entry 3: Received the signed medical authorization and initial urgent care notes. Records reference a concussion diagnosis and a recommendation for rest and follow-up with a primary care provider. Claimant has been advised that the carrier will need the follow-up treatment records to evaluate the injury component of the claim. Reviewing police report for liability details.

Entry 4: Claimant called to ask about the process and expressed concern about missing work. Explained that wage loss documentation from the employer will be required and that the claimant may keep receipts for any out-of-pocket medical costs. Recorded a recorded statement from the claimant regarding the sequence of events; claimant's account is consistent with the insured's reported position on the reversing maneuver.

Entry 5: Follow-up with the claimant's primary care provider's office confirmed an appointment is scheduled. Claimant reports symptoms have improved slightly but persist with screen use. Supervisor notified of the bodily injury component due to the concussion diagnosis. File remains open pending medical follow-up and liability review.
